text:
[
  {
    "n": 1,
    "kind": "Example",
    "title": "Empirical Heads Frequency",
    "source": "Lecture 1",
    "statement": "A coin is tossed 1000 times and lands on Heads 510 times. Find the empirical probability of getting Heads."
  },
  {
    "n": 2,
    "kind": "Example",
    "title": "Die Toss Sample Spaces",
    "source": "Lecture 1",
    "statement": "Determine the sample space when recording the exact number showing on a tossed die, and compare it with the sample space when recording only whether the number is even or odd."
  },
  {
    "n": 3,
    "kind": "Example",
    "title": "Component Lifetime Event",
    "source": "Lecture 1",
    "statement": "For a component whose lifetime in years has sample space S = {t | t >= 0}, describe the subset corresponding to the event that it fails before the end of the fifth year."
  },
  {
    "n": 4,
    "kind": "Example",
    "title": "Intersection of Student Attributes",
    "source": "Lecture 1",
    "statement": "Let E be the event that a randomly chosen student majors in engineering and F be the event that the student is female. Describe the event E \u2229 F."
  },
  {
    "n": 5,
    "kind": "Example",
    "title": "Desk Items Complement",
    "source": "Lecture 1",
    "statement": "Given the sample space S = {book, cell phone, mp3, paper, stationery, laptop} and event A = {book, stationery, laptop, paper}, determine the complement A'."
  },
  {
    "n": 6,
    "kind": "Example",
    "title": "Television Network Exclusivity",
    "source": "Lecture 1",
    "statement": "A cable package has eight channels across several networks, including ABC, NBC, and CBS. Determine whether selecting an NBC channel and selecting a CBS channel are mutually exclusive events."
  },
  {
    "n": 7,
    "kind": "Example",
    "title": "Union of Letter Sets",
    "source": "Lecture 1",
    "statement": "Find the union of the sets A = {a, b, c} and B = {b, c, d, e}."
  },
  {
    "n": 8,
    "kind": "Example",
    "title": "Union of Habits and Intervals",
    "source": "Lecture 1",
    "statement": "Characterize the union of employee smoking and drinking events, and find the union of open intervals (3, 9) and (5, 12)."
  },
  {
    "n": 9,
    "kind": "Example",
    "title": "At Least One Head in Two Tosses",
    "source": "Lecture 1",
    "statement": "A balanced coin is tossed twice. What is the probability that at least one head occurs?"
  },
  {
    "n": 10,
    "kind": "Example",
    "title": "Loaded Die Probability",
    "source": "Lecture 1",
    "statement": "A die is weighted so that an even number is twice as likely to occur as an odd number. Find the probability of rolling a number strictly less than 4."
  },
  {
    "n": 11,
    "kind": "Example",
    "title": "Union and Intersection on Loaded Die",
    "source": "Lecture 1",
    "statement": "On the weighted die where even outcomes are twice as likely as odd ones, let A be rolling an even number and B be rolling a multiple of 3. Find P(A \u222a B) and P(A \u2229 B)."
  },
  {
    "n": 12,
    "kind": "Example",
    "title": "Engineering Majors Selection",
    "source": "Lecture 1",
    "statement": "A class has 25 industrial, 10 mechanical, 10 electrical, and 8 civil engineering students. Find the probability that a randomly chosen student is (a) an industrial engineering major and (b) a civil or electrical engineering major."
  },
  {
    "n": 13,
    "kind": "Example",
    "title": "Job Offer Probabilities",
    "source": "Lecture 1",
    "statement": "A graduating student has probability 0.8 of an offer from company A, 0.6 from company B, and 0.5 from both. What is the probability of receiving at least one offer?"
  },
  {
    "n": 14,
    "kind": "Example",
    "title": "Sum of Seven or Eleven",
    "source": "Lecture 1",
    "statement": "What is the probability of rolling a total sum of 7 or 11 when a pair of fair dice is tossed?"
  },
  {
    "n": 15,
    "kind": "Example",
    "title": "Automobile Servicing Complement",
    "source": "Lecture 1",
    "statement": "A mechanic services 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, or 8+ cars with probabilities 0.12, 0.19, 0.28, 0.24, 0.10, and 0.07 respectively. What is the probability that he services at least 5 cars on a workday?"
  },
  {
    "n": 16,
    "kind": "Example",
    "title": "Single Die Roll Four",
    "source": "Lecture 1",
    "statement": "What is the probability of rolling a 4 on a fair six-sided die?"
  },
  {
    "n": 17,
    "kind": "Example",
    "title": "Meeting Probability Within Fifteen Minutes",
    "source": "Lecture 1",
    "statement": "Two friends arrive independently and uniformly at random at a meeting spot between 12:00 and 13:00, each waiting up to 15 minutes. What is the probability that they meet?"
  },
  {
    "n": 18,
    "kind": "Task",
    "title": "Three Coin Tosses",
    "source": "Tutorial 1",
    "statement": "For three tosses of a fair coin, specify the sample space, express events for exactly two heads, at least one head, and first toss head, compute their probabilities, and verify the addition rule."
  },
  {
    "n": 19,
    "kind": "Task",
    "title": "Server Cluster Operations and De Morgan Law",
    "source": "Tutorial 1",
    "statement": "In a three-server cluster, express in set operations the events that all servers are up, at least one is down, exactly one is up, and at least two are up, and prove De Morgan's law."
  },
  {
    "n": 20,
    "kind": "Task",
    "title": "Exam Passing Probabilities",
    "source": "Tutorial 1",
    "statement": "Given passing probabilities of 0.7 for Calculus, 0.6 for Linear Algebra, and 0.5 for both, find the probability of passing at least one, neither, exactly one, and Calculus but not Linear Algebra."
  },
  {
    "n": 21,
    "kind": "Task",
    "title": "Inclusion-Exclusion for Three Events",
    "source": "Tutorial 1",
    "statement": "Given probabilities of individual events, pairwise intersections, and the triple intersection for three events, compute the probability that at least one, none, at least two, and exactly one occur."
  },
  {
    "n": 22,
    "kind": "Task",
    "title": "Set Operations Probability Computations",
    "source": "Tutorial 1",
    "statement": "Given P(A) = 0.4, P(B) = 0.5, and P(A \u222a B) = 0.7, calculate P(A \u2229 B), P(A^c \u2229 B^c), P(A \\ B), P(A^c \u222a B^c), and P(A \u0394 B)."
  },
  {
    "n": 23,
    "kind": "Task",
    "title": "Defective Items Sampling Without Replacement",
    "source": "Tutorial 1",
    "statement": "Four items are drawn without replacement from a batch of 10 items containing 3 defectives. Find the probabilities of getting zero, exactly one, and at least one defective item."
  },
  {
    "n": 24,
    "kind": "Task",
    "title": "Meeting Time and Waiting Duration",
    "source": "Tutorial 1",
    "statement": "Two people arrive uniformly between 12:00 and 13:00 waiting 15 minutes; find the probability they meet, and determine the required waiting time for the meeting probability to be at least 1/2."
  },
  {
    "n": 25,
    "kind": "Task",
    "title": "Broken Stick Triangle Condition",
    "source": "Tutorial 1",
    "statement": "A stick of unit length is broken at two uniformly and independently chosen points. Find the probability that the three resulting segments can form a triangle."
  },
  {
    "n": 26,
    "kind": "Task",
    "title": "Axiom Verification on Finite Space",
    "source": "Tutorial 1",
    "statement": "Determine which of four specified set functions on a four-element sample space is a valid probability measure, identifying the failing axiom for invalid candidates and computing probabilities for the valid one."
  },
  {
    "n": 27,
    "kind": "Task",
    "title": "Geometric Weights and Finite-Infinite Measures",
    "source": "Tutorial 1",
    "statement": "Determine the normalizing constant c for P({k}) = c/3^k on natural numbers, find probabilities of even outcomes and k >= 3, and test if indicator Q(A) of set infinitude is a probability measure."
  },
  {
    "n": 28,
    "kind": "Task",
    "title": "Sigma-Algebra Identification and Generation",
    "source": "Tutorial 1",
    "statement": "Check whether four candidate collections of subsets on a four-element set are sigma-algebras, and construct the minimal sigma-algebra generated by two singleton sets."
  },
  {
    "n": 29,
    "kind": "Task",
    "title": "Axiomatic Probability and Sigma-Algebra Properties",
    "source": "Tutorial 1",
    "statement": "Prove P(\u2205) = 0 and monotonicity from Kolmogorov axioms, prove that the intersection of two sigma-algebras is a sigma-algebra, and provide a counterexample showing the union need not be."
  }
]
